title: Tale of the Simpleton Husband
summary: In an isolated mountain village where polished glass was unknown, an honest peasant named Mansur visited the city of Aleppo for the first...
full_text:
In an isolated mountain village where polished glass was unknown, an honest peasant named Mansur visited the city of Aleppo for the first time. In the bazaar, he found a small silver pocket mirror dropped by a traveling merchant.

Mansur picked up the mirror, looked into the polished surface, and gasped in astonishment: 'Praise be to heaven! It is a portrait of my beloved late father, looking young and handsome as in his youth!'

He kissed the glass with filial devotion, wrapped it in silk, and hid it in a cedar chest beneath his bed, visiting it secretly every evening to speak to 'his father.'

His wife, noticing his secretive visits to the chest, waited until Mansur went to the fields, unlocked the coffer, and looked into the mirror!

She shrieked in horror: 'Aha! The traitor has hidden the portrait of an ugly, scowling rival woman inside my chest!'

She ran weeping to the village judge, demanding a divorce!

The judge took the silver mirror, looked into the surface, stroked his long white beard, and frowned with solemn authority: 'Woman, your jealousy has blinded your eyes! This is neither a rival woman nor his father; this is a sacred portrait of the Chief Judge of Aleppo, wearing a splendid scholar’s turban!'

The village schoolmaster entered the courtroom, saw the dispute, laughed heartily, and explained the scientific mystery of reflection.

He held the mirror before the husband, wife, and judge together, showing them their own faces laughing in the glass!

The couple embraced in joyful relief, learning that ignorance creates monsters out of shadows, while knowledge brings light and peace.
moral: Ignorance creates imaginary rivals out of ordinary objects; knowledge dispels baseless fears.
